title: A timer that never fires shows up as an activation failure, not a missed run
explanation: `systemctl status cleanup.timer` shows it failed to activate at all: `Failed to start cleanup.timer: Invalid argument`. That's systemd's own parser rejecting the unit's schedule, not the cleanup job itself failing — `cleanup.service` and its `ExecStart` script are never even reached.

title: OnCalendar= is a strict grammar, not free text
explanation: `cat /etc/systemd/system/cleanup.timer` shows `OnCalendar=daily at 3am` — readable to a human, but not valid systemd calendar-event syntax. systemd doesn't attempt to interpret loose English; an expression it can't parse just makes the whole timer unit fail to activate, silently as far as any downstream consumer is concerned.

title: Know the real grammar and validate before committing
explanation: systemd calendar expressions follow `Weekday YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`, with `*` meaning "any" in a field — daily at 3am is `OnCalendar=*-*-* 03:00:00` (or the `daily` shorthand for midnight). `systemd-analyze calendar '*-*-* 03:00:00'` prints the next several times an expression would actually fire, which is the fast way to catch a bad expression before it ships instead of after someone notices a job never ran.

title: Fix, reload, and restart — both are needed here
explanation: After correcting the `OnCalendar=` line, `systemctl daemon-reload` picks up the edited unit file, and `systemctl restart cleanup.timer` is needed on top of that because the timer previously failed to activate at all — there's no already-running instance to simply pick up the new config.

title: Confirm there's a real next trigger time, not just that the unit loaded
explanation: `systemctl list-timers cleanup.timer` (or `systemctl status cleanup.timer`) showing an actual `NEXT` timestamp is the real proof — a schedule that parses cleanly and one that silently never fires can otherwise look identical from a quick glance at `is-active`, since a timer unit can be `active` while still holding an expression that resolves to no future occurrence.
